This prompt is your whole context: do not open plan, spec or todo files, and perform only the work described here. You write tests only; no production code.

Background: KyberDash (dash/) turns each harness model call into a canonical record with a span id `synth:<harness>:<native session>:<native record id>`. When a call has no stable native id, `nativeRecordIdentity` in dash/src/synth/synth.ts falls back to sha256(session, timestamp, "llm.invoke", ordinal), and the ordinal is the call's index in the whole windowed batch. The refresh window start moves every run, so the same call is re-minted under a new id and duplicate rows pile up. Kilo hits this because its SQLite parser reads a root session plus its child (subagent) sessions and keys child calls `kilo-code:<child session>:<message id>`, which fails the `${provider}:${sessionId}:` prefix check (sessionId is the root). The fix (next task, not yours) makes the ordinal the occurrence index among calls with the same native session id and the same timestamp, and has the Kilo parser stamp each call's message id as a new identity-only field `recordIdentity`.

Files:
- dash/src/synth/synth.test.ts: add describe "record identity is window-independent". Use Synthesizer.synthesizeEnvelopes and Synthesizer.synthesize with hand-built ParsedProviderCall values whose deduplicationKey does NOT start with `${provider}:${sessionId}:` and that carry no turnId. Assert hash-backed calls get the same span ids when the batch is [other-session call, A@t1, B@t2, C@t2] and when it is [B@t2, C@t2], and that B and C still get different ids. Cover both methods.
- dash/src/providers/kilo-code.test.ts: add describe "kilo child-session record identity". Reuse the file's existing kilo.db fixture builder; add a root session, one child session (parent_id = root) and assistant messages in both. Parse through createKiloCodeProvider(...).createSessionParser and derive ids with spanIdFor (exported from dash/src/synth/synth.ts) under harness `kilo-shared-runtime`. Assert: the child message's span id is `synth:kilo-shared-runtime:<root>:<msg.id>` and is identical whether or not an earlier message is inside the window; a root message's span id stays `...:<msg.id>` as today; pairingId is still the message id.

Constraints: no test opens ~/.kyberdash/canon.db or the real ~/.local/share/kilo; use temporary fixtures only.

Command (from the repository root; paths after `--` are relative to dash/):
`scripts/proc-guard.sh run -- npm --prefix dash run test:related -- src/synth/synth.test.ts src/providers/kilo-code.test.ts`

Acceptance criteria: both new describes exist and FAIL for the intended reason (span ids differ between the two batches; the Kilo child message id is a 16-hex hash), all pre-existing tests in both files still pass, the run reports a non-zero test count, and the failing output is pasted into your digest as RED evidence. Background: the KyberDash canonical store (dash/src/canon/store.ts, CanonStore) holds duplicate copies of model-call records that earlier refreshes re-minted under new hash-based ids. A hash-backed record carries `raw.provenance.recordDigest`; a record with a stable native id does not. Each copy's `record_provenance.imported_at_utc` is the import that wrote it. The fix (later task) adds two things: (1) CanonStore.commitSourceUnit deletes, in its transaction, every existing `llm.invoke` row of the same harness and source key whose timestamp equals one in the batch, whose span id is not in the batch, and which is hash-backed, together with its `tool.invoke` children (by parent_span_id) and the provenance rows of every deleted span; (2) a schema migration 23 -> 24 (MIGRATIONS[23]) that, for file-sourced (`source LIKE 'codeburn/%'`) `llm.invoke` rows grouped by harness, session_id, timestamp and name spanning more than one imported_at_utc, keeps every row of the latest import and deletes the hash-backed rows of older imports with their tool children and provenance, then increments the RECORDS_WRITE_MARKER_KEY metadata value. It is idempotent and has a blocking form (store constructor) and a yielding form (migrateCanonDatabase).

Files:
- dash/src/canon/store-supersede.test.ts (new), describe "commitSourceUnit supersedes hash-backed copies", against new CanonStore(':memory:'). Committing a unit with calls at t1 deletes an older hash-backed row of the same harness and source key at t1 that the batch lacks, with its tool child and provenance; it keeps a stable-id row at t1, a hash-backed row at t0, and a hash-backed row at t1 under another source key.
- dash/src/canon/migration-v24.test.ts (new), describe "v23 -> v24 duplicate record repair", modelled on dash/src/canon/migration-v23.test.ts: build the store in a mkdtempSync directory, stamp schema_version 23, insert (a) a Kilo-shaped group of three hash-backed copies from three imports, each with a tool child, (b) a Cursor-shaped group of two distinct calls per import over two imports, (c) a single-import group of distinct same-instant calls, (d) a stable-id row across imports. Reopen with CanonStore: schema 24, only the latest import's copies of (a) and (b) remain, (c) and (d) untouched, children and provenance of deleted rows gone, records write marker incremented. Running MIGRATIONS[23] again changes nothing. A separate case runs migrateCanonDatabase and asserts the identical surviving rows. Import MIGRATIONS, SCHEMA_VERSION and RECORDS_WRITE_MARKER_KEY from dash/src/canon/store.ts.

Constraints: never open ~/.kyberdash/canon.db; temporary stores only.

Command (from the repository root):
`scripts/proc-guard.sh run -- npm --prefix dash run test:related -- src/canon/store-supersede.test.ts src/canon/migration-v24.test.ts`

Acceptance criteria: both files exist and FAIL for the intended reason (old copies survive the commit; SCHEMA_VERSION is 23 and MIGRATIONS[23] is undefined), the run reports a non-zero test count, and the failing output is pasted into your digest as RED evidence. This prompt is your whole context: do not open plan, spec or todo files, and perform only the work described here. You write tests only.

Background: the KyberDash refresh dies with a JavaScript heap out-of-memory in buildRuns (dash/src/canon/runs.ts): its persist loop loads every record of a run with CanonStore.recordsForSession / recordsForShare, then deriveOutcome (dash/src/canon/outcome.ts) reads each record's content and parts. Those are lazy fields (defineLazy in dash/src/canon/store-rows.ts) that cache the decompressed text until released (assigning undefined releases; releaseRecordParts does it for parts and content), so a 15,000-record session keeps 1.33 GB live. The fix (later task) makes deriveOutcome take any iterable, read each record once and release its parts before the next, and adds generators CanonStore.iterateRecordsForSession(key) and CanonStore.iterateRecordsForShare(key, harness) that buildRuns streams through.

Files:
- dash/src/canon/outcome.test.ts: add describe "deriveOutcome memory bound". Build 200 records whose parts and content are instrumented getter/setter properties following the defineLazy contract (compute on first read, an undefined assignment releases), counting inflations live at once. Assert peak live inflated parts is at most 1, none remain live after deriveOutcome returns, deriveOutcome accepts a generator, and the returned block deep-equals the block for the same records built with plain (eager) parts and content: errors, user corrections, test deltas and termination.
- dash/src/canon/runs.test.ts: add describe "buildRuns streams outcome records". Use an in-memory CanonStore subclass whose iterateRecordsForSession and iterateRecordsForShare yield instrumented records for a seeded session; call buildRuns(store); assert peak live inflated parts during the run phase is at most 1 and that the stored run outcome (read with CanonStore.listRuns, the accessor the file already uses) equals deriveOutcome over the same records as an array.
